## Findings

**1. The designed order, line 115; The scenes, line 161; The designed order, line 111 (ruling 5, "The hidden position").** Read together, the two pasted sentences do not settle when the next carrier stands there after the carrier's own patient has come in: at the moment of that coming in a carrier does stand there (the one touched), so "whenever a patient comes in and no carrier stands there" can be read as "only at the next coming in from the door", which leaves no carrier for a whole cycle and makes "a carrier stands" and "the child may always choose it" untrue. Three further doubts follow from the same sentences: whether a standing carrier stays when the position reaches the last one or drops below `basket` (no saved list removes it, so it stays); the beats of scene 4 send in "the one who waited" even when the carrier was touched, against "the one who waits stays where it is"; and with the carrier laid out from the same stream in the same coming in, "the patient laid out next" in line 111 is now the carrier's patient, who by the first half of that sentence cannot have the new need. The reading chosen is the one that keeps the option always there: the next carrier is laid out at once, as part of the same coming in.

Replace line 115 with:

> - **A harder option the child picks.** A carrier stands beside the one who waits, shut, with two eyes at its window. Its patient is laid out from the same stream, by the same rules as any other patient and one position above the position stored at that moment, at each coming in at which the stored position is `basket` or later and not the last and no carrier would otherwise stand there afterwards. That is so when the one who waits comes in and no carrier stands there, and when the carrier's own patient comes in: the next carrier is laid out as part of that same coming in, and a shut carrier stands there again before that patient is on the table. A carrier that stands keeps its patient until the child touches it, whatever the stored position does meanwhile. It looks harder because less of the animal can be seen, and whenever a patient can come in (the table empty, or the patient on it well) the child may choose it by touching it; the one who waits stays where it is. A carrier cycle is judged like any other.

Replace line 161 with:

> 4. **Coming in** (3 to 4 seconds, and never in the way of a touch). *Cause:* with the table empty or the patient on it well, the child touches the one who waits, or the carrier. While a need on the table is unmet, a touch on either is answered where it stands (the one who waits looks up and shows its sign once more, the eyes at the window blink) and nobody comes in. *Beats:* the animal on the table hops down and goes out to the garden with what helped it, its own to keep; the one who was touched comes in the way its need makes it move, from the door or out of the carrier, and climbs onto the table; the cart rolls in behind it, carrying every thing of the new layout; when it came out of the carrier, the open carrier slides out and a shut one slides in where it stood, before the patient is on the table. *Saved when the scene starts:* `garden` (the animal that goes out and what helped it; a fourth pushes the oldest out), `table` (the one who comes in), `finished` (cleared), `waiting` and `drawn` when the one at the door came in (the next patient, laid out from the stored position; a touch on the carrier leaves `waiting` as it was), `carrier` and `drawn` (when the carrier was touched, the next carrier's patient, or none where "A harder option the child picks" lays none out; when the one at the door came in and no carrier stood there, a carrier's patient as that rule says; otherwise unchanged), and `things` (each thing the new cart carries lies on the cart again). `made` is not changed: what was made of a thing comes in with it.

In line 111 replace "and the patient laid out next has the new need" with:

> and the next patient laid out for the door has the new need

(How the open carrier leaves and the shut one arrives is the builder's to draw; what the replacement fixes is that it happens inside the same scene and that `carrier` is written in the same save.)

**2. Where the two differ, line 213; The claim, line 223; The records, line 173 (ruling 10).** "Named by no record" and "only water is named by a record" speak for the whole pack and are not true of it: in the `preschool-tk` practical life and feelings lane of this very band, records the sheet does not name (Health, Strand 1.0, codes 1.2, 1.8 and 1.9) name feeling unwell or uncomfortable, thirst and tiredness in the child's own body, and `us-ca 1.2.1.G` in a grade 1 lane names sleep and rest.

In line 213 replace "are named by no record" with:

> are named by none of the records above

In line 223 replace "of the five cares, only water is named by a record." with:

> of the five cares, only the bowl of water is taken from a record.

In line 173 replace "of the five cares, only water is named by a record." with:

> of the five cares, only the bowl of water is taken from a record.

("Rest on no record" in lines 215 and 223 stands: it says what the game rests on, not what the pack holds.)

**3. The grid, line 54.** "Its sign" and "the one thing that would fit its need" are written for one need, but at `two` and `two-quiet` the one who waits has two needs and two things that fit. Replace the last two sentences of the line (from "The one who waits takes a thing as play" to the end) with:

> The one who waits takes a thing as play, by its taste, and each sign it shows stays at its step whatever it is given: a need is met on the table only. A thing that would fit a need it has is never used on it there: held out at the door, it is sniffed and nosed back toward the table, so the care that fits is never seen not to help.
